title: Headless CMS
seoTitle: What Is a Headless CMS? Explained for Business Owners
seoDescription: A headless CMS stores content separately from the website that displays it. Benefits for speed and multiple channels, trade-offs, costs and when it fits.
summary: A headless CMS is a content system that stores and manages content but does not decide how it looks; developers fetch the content through an API and display it on a fast custom website, app or other channel. It trades some editing convenience for speed, security and flexibility.

dataPoints.label: Benefits
dataPoints.value: Faster sites, fewer security risks, one content source for web, app and more

dataPoints.label: Trade-offs
dataPoints.value: Page previews and layout changes need developer set-up

dataPoints.label: Suits
dataPoints.value: Growing companies with frequent content, multiple channels or performance targets

body:
## How it differs from WordPress

In a traditional CMS, content and page templates live together. In a headless set-up, editors work in the CMS while the website, often built with a framework such as Next.js, fetches content through an [API](/glossary/api).

## Is it right for you

If your site is small and rarely changes, a traditional CMS is simpler. If speed, several channels or a design system matter, headless is worth it. See [headless CMS for growing companies](/blog/headless-cms-for-growing-companies).

faqs.q: Do editors find headless CMSs harder?
faqs.a: Slightly at first, especially for page layouts, but good set-ups include live previews and reusable blocks.

faqs.q: Is a headless site better for SEO?
faqs.a: It can be faster, which helps, but SEO depends on content, structure and technical set-up, not the CMS alone.
